story.speaker: Nova
story.message: Welcome to Data Delta! Data is just information we can collect and study.

story.speaker: Nova
story.message: Your height, your favorite games, the weather today — all of it is data.

story.speaker: Pixel
story.message: Once we collect data, we can find patterns in it!

concept.title: What is data?
concept.explanation: Data is information collected for analysis — numbers, words, or categories. Analysts look for patterns inside it.
concept.example: Favorite colors of 5 friends: Red, Blue, Blue, Green, Blue

playground.instructions: Tap to collect sample data points and watch a simple tally build up.

challenge.prompt: Which of these is an example of data?
options: The number of pets each classmate has

story.speaker: Nova
story.message: Raw data is messy. Sorting it makes patterns easier to see.

story.speaker: Nova
story.message: We can sort numbers from smallest to largest, or group words by category.

story.speaker: Pixel
story.message: Sorted data is so much easier to read!

concept.title: Sorting data
concept.explanation: Sorting arranges data in order — like smallest to largest — so it's easier to spot the highest, lowest, or middle value.

playground.instructions: Drag the number cards into order from smallest to largest.

challenge.prompt: Arrange these numbers from smallest to largest: 8, 3, 5, 1

story.speaker: Nova
story.message: The average tells us a typical value for a whole group of numbers.

story.speaker: Nova
story.message: Add all the numbers together, then divide by how many numbers there are.

story.speaker: Pixel
story.message: Averages help us compare groups fairly!

concept.title: The average (mean)
concept.explanation: To find the average: add up all the values, then divide by the count of values.

playground.instructions: Add your own numbers and watch the average update live.

challenge.prompt: What is the average of 4, 8, and 12?

story.speaker: Nova
story.message: Numbers in a list are hard to compare. Charts make patterns jump out instantly.

story.speaker: Nova
story.message: A bar chart uses taller bars for bigger values — easy to compare at a glance.

story.speaker: Pixel
story.message: One good chart is worth a hundred rows of numbers!

concept.title: Reading bar charts
concept.explanation: A bar chart represents each value as a bar — the taller the bar, the bigger the value. This makes comparing values fast and visual.
concept.example: Apples: 5 -> short bar.  Bananas: 9 -> tall bar.

playground.instructions: Drag the values to build bars and see which category has the most.

challenge.prompt: In a bar chart, what does a taller bar mean?

story.speaker: Nova
story.message: You've learned data, sorting, averages, and charts. Time for a full analysis!

story.speaker: Nova
story.message: A good analyst collects data, sorts it, finds the average, then charts the result to tell the story.

story.speaker: Pixel
story.message: This is the Boss Challenge — analyze a real survey from start to finish!

concept.title: The analysis pipeline
concept.explanation: A full data analysis follows steps in order: collect the data, sort or clean it, calculate summary stats like the average, then visualize it with a chart.
concept.example: Collect scores -> sort them -> average = sum / count -> draw a bar chart.

playground.instructions: Walk through analyzing a class survey: collect, sort, average, then chart the results.

challenge.prompt: Put the steps of a data analysis in the correct order.
